turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I'm okay, I think. A bit sleepy still, but not too bad.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good to hear. Can you tell me your pain level on a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 is no pain and 10 is the worst pain?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Maybe around 3 or 4? It's more like a dull ache, not sharp.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Alright, we can manage that with medication. Are you feeling any nausea or did you have any vomiting after waking up?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I haven't vomited, but I feel a bit queasy. Like my stomach is upset.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. We'll keep an eye on that and give you something to help if needed. How's your breathing? Any shortness of breath or wheezing?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I'm breathing fine. Just a bit tired from the anesthesia, I guess.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Since you have mild asthma, we want to make sure there's no reaction. Do you remember anything from the operating room or waking up?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Not really. I remember going to sleep and then waking up here. It's all a bit fuzzy.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's normal with general anesthesia. We also gave you a spinal, so your lower body might feel a bit heavy still. Any concerns or questions for me?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I think that's all. Just want to go home soon.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: We'll get you ready for that soon. Rest well and let the nurses know if you need anything.
